case_metadata.participant_note: All participant-visible evidence for this case is frozen in the evidence directory. Hidden keys are stored outside the repository.

evidence.content:
Corruption occurs only for uploads larger than 8 MiB using content-encoding zstd.
Small uploads and large uncompressed uploads are unaffected.
Affected requests all traversed proxy firmware 7.4.

Client library 5.0 introduced zstd-by-default for payloads >8 MiB.
Proxy firmware 7.4 was rolled to half the gateway fleet.
Older client 4.8 does not send zstd. Proxy 7.3 and 7.4 both pass ordinary chunked uploads.

On the failing 5.0 + 7.4 path, the proxy emits a malformed final chunk after zstd streaming crosses the 8 MiB internal buffer boundary.
The same client stream captured before proxy ingress has a valid checksum.

Routing client-5.0 traffic through proxy-7.3 eliminates corruption.
Keeping proxy-7.4 but disabling zstd on client-5.0 also eliminates corruption.
Neither mitigation changes document content before gateway processing.

candidates.claim: The client library is the root cause because it introduced the zstd encoding that triggers the failure condition (payloads > 8 MiB). Without this change, the corruption does not occur regardless of the proxy version (as seen in E02 and E03). It is the 'enabling' change that introduced the new behavior into the ecosystem.

The proxy firmware is the root cause because it contains the specific bug that corrupts zstd-encoded streams exceeding 8 MiB (as seen in E04). The proxy is the 'executing' change that performs the actual corruption; proxy 7.3 handles the same client-5.0 zstd streams successfully (as seen in E03).

candidate_causes.claim: The client library is the root cause because it introduced the zstd encoding that triggers the failure condition (payloads > 8 MiB). Without this change, the corruption does not occur regardless of the proxy version (as seen in E02 and E03). It is the 'enabling' change that introduced the new behavior into the ecosystem.

The proxy firmware is the root cause because it contains the specific bug that corrupts zstd-encoded streams exceeding 8 MiB (as seen in E04). The proxy is the 'executing' change that performs the actual corruption; proxy 7.3 handles the same client-5.0 zstd streams successfully (as seen in E03).

action.recommended_action: Roll back proxy firmware to 7.3 or disable zstd encoding on client library 5.0.
action.reason: Both actions are verified in E05 to eliminate corruption without altering document content. Rolling back the proxy is the preferred fix for the underlying bug, while disabling zstd is a viable immediate mitigation to restore service for large uploads while the proxy bug is patched.

evidence.claim: The issue is specific to the combination of client 5.0 (zstd) and proxy 7.4. Client 4.8 (no zstd) works on both proxies, and client 5.0 (zstd) works on proxy 7.3.
The proxy firmware 7.4 is the point of failure, as it emits a malformed final chunk after the 8 MiB buffer boundary is crossed.
Both isolating the traffic to proxy 7.3 and disabling zstd on the client successfully eliminate the corruption.

uncertainty: While the proxy is the site of corruption, the client library is the reason the corruption is now visible in production. The 'root cause' is a dependency between a new client feature and a proxy bug.

next_test.test: Deploy a hotfix to proxy firmware 7.4 that correctly handles zstd streaming beyond the 8 MiB buffer boundary and verify with a synthetic 12 MiB zstd upload.
next_test.outcome_a_implication: If the hotfix passes, the proxy firmware bug is confirmed as the primary technical failure.
next_test.outcome_b_implication: If the hotfix fails, the buffer handling logic may have deeper architectural issues.
